meta.source: Spider (Yu et al., 2018) dev-set questions + official gold SQL, xlangai/spider HuggingFace mirror -- verbatim, third-party authored, not hand-written for this project.
meta.purpose: Third evaluation domain (tennis), selected via scripts/rank_all_spider_databases.py for join-free-friendliness against planner/'s 4-operator vocabulary.
meta.selection_note: 62 real dev-set questions covering 31 distinct gold queries (2.00x paraphrase density -- exactly 2 phrasings per underlying query). Deduplicated to 31 by gold SQL text (first-occurrence phrasing kept). All 25 single-table queries kept; 5 of 6 multi-table/compound queries kept as deliberate refusal cases (1 dropped for being a shape-duplicate: two near-identical players+rankings JOIN GROUP BY first_name queries differing only in aggregate function -- kept the more commonly-asked 'average' form, dropped 'total'). No questions authored, reworded, or padded.
meta.tiers: SQL-structural (filter/aggregate/group_by/order_by/multi_or_compound), not this project's T1-T5 op-count scheme -- Spider's SQL wasn't authored against planner/'s operator vocabulary, so re-deriving an op-count tier would require subjective reinterpretation of third-party content.
meta.single_table_register_note: Originally selected against the domain's full multi-table schema; converted to a single-table register ('matches') to match register.pkl/employees.pkl's convention (zero engine changes needed). 11 previously-answerable queries that touched a different table were converted to refusal cases -- the underlying gold SQL is kept for documentation, but is not executed (expected_behavior=refuse).
meta.tier_convention_note: 'tier' distinguishes answer vs refuse queries for reporting (mirrors eval_corpus.json/eval_corpus_employee.json's out_of_range convention -- never pooled into one blended accuracy number). Deliberately NOT labeled 'out_of_range': that tier means unanswerable IN PRINCIPLE (undefined terms, no such column/data at all); these refuse-cases are answerable in principle but need a table outside this domain's single-table register -- a different mechanism, kept a different label. 'sql_structure' preserves the original filter/aggregate/group_by/order_by/multi_or_compound classification for every query (answer and refuse alike).

queries.question: List the names of all winners who played in both 2013 and 2016.
queries.gold_sql: SELECT winner_name FROM matches WHERE YEAR  =  2013 INTERSECT SELECT winner_name FROM matches WHERE YEAR  =  2016
queries.retier_note: 2026-10-01 (decision D7): in scope = answerable from the data provided. The gold SQL is a single-table INTERSECT over the register (matches), so the question is answerable and in scope; INTERSECT is outside the four-operator vocabulary, so it is out_of_contract_aggregate (beyond the vocabulary), not out_of_scope_register. Was: expected_behavior refuse, reason 'requires a multi-table join or set operation (INTERSECT)'.

queries.question: What are the country code and first name of the players who won in both tourney WTA Championships and Australian Open?
queries.gold_sql: SELECT T1.country_code ,  T1.first_name FROM players AS T1 JOIN matches AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.winner_id WHERE T2.tourney_name  =  'WTA Championships' INTERSECT SELECT T1.country_code ,  T1.first_name FROM players AS T1 JOIN matches AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.winner_id WHERE T2.tourney_name  =  'Australian Open'
queries.reason: requires a multi-table join or set operation (INTERSECT); planner/'s 4 operators (filter, select, aggregate, compute) have no join or set-operation primitive.

queries.gold_sql: SELECT T1.country_code ,  T1.first_name FROM players AS T1 JOIN rankings AS T2 ON T1.player_id  =  T2.player_id ORDER BY T2.tours DESC LIMIT 1
